channel.title: Salt Lake Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Salt Lake Tribune (sltrib.com)

item.title: LDS Church advises its thousands of members in the Middle East to stay put as ‘safest’ option
item.description: Latter-day Saints in the Middle East and students and faculty at BYU's Jerusalem Center are sheltering in place rather than evacuating in the midst of the Iran war.

item.title: She wanted to protest ICE. Her Utah city tried to charge her $2K to do it.
item.description: Legal experts say a Utah city's attempt to charge a resident $2,000 in police fees to hold a protest was unconstitutional.

item.title: Utah taxpayers will fund a $100K mail-in voting ‘security’ study after a GOP election bill fails
item.description: After a GOP proposal that would have added barriers to voting by mail failed, Utah lawmakers passed a last-minute bill to fund a study of mail-in voting “security."

item.title: Bagley Cartoon: All Up in Your Business
item.description: Check out Pat Bagley's latest cartoon: All Up in Your Business

item.title: How Utah’s state employee benefits will likely change this year
item.description: Two bills that Gov. Spencer Cox said would improve Utah's state employees' benefits have passed the Legislature.

item.title: Here’s why Utah lawmakers again refused to expand E-Verify, which checks worker citizenship status
item.description: The second attempt in as many years failed, despite practically zero public pushback from industries this year.

item.title: ‘It’s not a mild virus, it’s a severe illness,’ Utah health officials warn as measles cases keep climbing
item.description: Measles cases continue to climb across Utah, with more than 350 infections reported since June. Health officials say many underestimate how severe the virus can be.

item.title: Man accused of 3 Utah killings will fight being returned to the state ‘every step of the way,’ lawyer says
item.description: Ivan Miller, arrested Thursday in Colorado, "will not be waiving" his right to hearings there and will dispute being returned to Utah, Durango public defender Scott Van Zandt said.

item.title: Utah will sell part of the Great Salt Lake to the feds — a deal lawmakers call a ‘win-win’ for the lake
item.description: After more than a decade of legal fights, Utah has agreed to sell 22,311 acres of the Great Salt Lake’s lakebed to the federal government in exchange for more than $60 million.

item.title: A bar right by Sugar House Park? Utah’s latest booze bill could allow it — but there’s a catch.
item.description: The annual effort to tweak Utah’s liquor laws could make plans for a boutique hotel right by Sugar House Park boozier — plus a few other proposed changes.
